bib.title: Stop Overthinking: A Survey on Efficient Reasoning for Large Language Models

question: What approaches exist for making long chain-of-thought reasoning models reason efficiently, cutting verbose output while keeping accuracy?
contributions: First structured survey of efficient reasoning in LLMs, with three categories: model-based, reasoning output-based, input prompts-based
Covers efficient training data, small-model reasoning, evaluation and benchmarks

results.claim: Illustrative overthinking example: DeepSeek-R1 takes 602 words and 42 seconds to compare 0.9 and 0.11.
results.setup: One prompt 'Which is larger, 0.9 or 0.11?', one run, tested March 2025; an illustration, not a measurement.

results.claim: Same example on QwQ-32B: 616 words and 19 seconds.
Survey cites o1 output price as a cost motive for efficient reasoning.
results.setup: No citation given; price as of the survey's writing, now dated.
results.quote: OpenAI o1 costs $60 per 1M generated tokens

results.claim: Agentic overthinking: lower overthinking scores select better solutions and cut compute.
results.source: Cuadron et al. 2025, The danger of overthinking [29]
results.setup: 4,018 agentic trajectories; model and tasks not named in the survey; selecting lower-overthinking-score solutions.
results.quote: can improve performance by 30% and at the same time reduce computational overhead by 43%

results.claim: Number of agentic trajectories analysed in the overthinking study.
results.quote: By examining 4,018 trajectories in agentic tasks

results.claim: Longer CoT does not always help: accuracy rises then falls; an optimal length depends on model capability and task difficulty.
results.source: Wu et al. 2025, More is less / length-filtered vote [193]
results.setup: Mathematical analysis plus a length-filtered voting method; no numbers given in the survey.
results.quote: performance initially improves but eventually declines due to error accumulation

results.claim: Prompt-based compression falls far short of information-theoretic limits on the accuracy-compression trade-off.
results.setup: Prompts like 'use 10 words or less'; different prompts lie on one accuracy-length curve.
results.quote: existing prompt-based compression methods fall far short of these limits

results.claim: Chain of Draft prompt caps each thinking step at five words; survey says it preserves accuracy and reduces tokens, without figures.
results.source: Xu et al. 2025, Chain of Draft [204]
results.quote: this approach preserves the necessary intermediate steps while maintaining accuracy, significantly reducing token usage

results.claim: Token-budget prompting: LLM estimates its own budget (TALE-EP), training-free and zero-shot.
results.source: Han et al. 2024, Token-budget-aware LLM reasoning [58]
results.quote: TALE-EP, a training-free, zero-shot method for budget estimation

results.claim: With suitable test-time scaling, a 1B model can beat a 405B model on MATH-500.
results.source: Liu et al. 2025, Can 1B LLM surpass 405B [113]
results.setup: Compute-optimal TTS depends on policy model, process reward model and difficulty.
results.quote: smaller models (e.g., a 1B parameter LLM) are able to outperform significantly larger models (e.g., a 405B parameter LLM) on complex reasoning tasks like MATH-500

results.claim: LIMO: 817 curated samples outperform models trained on over 100,000.
results.setup: Reasoning fine-tuning; no benchmark named in the survey.
results.quote: with only 817 carefully selected training samples, LIMO can outperform previous models that utilized over 100,000 examples

results.claim: s1K dataset of 1,000 questions with budget forcing; s1-32B exceeds o1-preview on MATH and AIME24.
results.setup: SFT on s1K plus budget forcing at inference.
results.quote: comprising 1,000 high-quality questions paired with reasoning traces

results.claim: S2R: 3,100 initialization samples for self-verification and self-correction, then RL.
results.setup: Qwen2.5-Math-7B outperforms comparable long-CoT distilled models on MATH500 and GSM8K.

results.claim: LoRA tunes a small fraction of parameters when adapting to short reasoning.
results.setup: General statement about the SFT line of work.
results.quote: with less than 1% of the parameters tuned

results.claim: Quantization preserves small-model reasoning; pruning degrades it severely.
results.quote: pruning, which removes specific weights or neurons in the model based on their importance, leads to severe degradation in reasoning quality

results.claim: Looping a k-layer transformer L times can emulate a kL-layer model.
results.quote: looping a k-layer transformer L times can emulate the performance of a kL-layer model

results.claim: R1-Zero shows longer responses correlate with better benchmark performance during training, so efficiency work runs against training recipes.
results.quote: exhibits a direct correlation between increased training duration with longer response lengths and improved benchmark performance

results.claim: Reasoning models given questions missing key information keep thinking rather than admit failure.
results.quote: they tend to keep “thinking” over and over instead of admitting they fail to answer

results.claim: Sys2Bench finds no single inference-time technique wins across all reasoning tasks.
results.setup: Eleven datasets across five reasoning categories.
results.quote: no single technique consistently excels across all reasoning tasks

limits: Survey with no experiments of its own; only Fig 4 (one prompt, March 2025) and the o1 price are its own, and the survey gives no comparison table of accuracy or token savings across methods.
No limitations section; the authors concede 'efficient reasoning remains in the early stages of research' (abstract) and that o1's mechanism is unconfirmed (p5 footnote).
RL versus SFT is left open: 'the answer is unclear as each method has its own strengths' (p20).
Relayed numbers are unchecked against the originals; the model and tasks behind several relayed results are not named.
Coverage ends around August 2025 (v4); the $60 price and the March 2025 timings are dated; only Claude 3.7 Sonnet is covered as a hybrid reasoning model.
Absolute claim without evidence: safety and efficiency trade off, 'optimizing one always leads to the performance degradation of the other' (p19).
Applications (driving, embodied AI, healthcare, recommenders) are prospective prose without data.
practices: Prompt-guided efficiency: state a token budget in the prompt (p14), cap each step at five words (Chain of Draft, Table 5), or add 'Be concise' (CCoT, Table 5).
Estimate a per-question token budget by asking the model first (TALE-EP, p14).
Route easy queries to a fast model and hard ones to a reasoning model (Sec 5.2, p15).
Prefer combining RL and SFT for efficient reasoning models, since RL is adaptive and SFT stable (Sec 8.2, p20).
Use test-time scaling selectively with early stopping (Speculative Rejection, ST-BoN, Dynasor) to limit inference cost (Sec 4.2, pp11-13).

terms.definition: situations where LLMs generate excessively detailed or unnecessarily elaborate reasoning steps, ultimately reducing their problem-solving efficiency
optimize reasoning length while preserving reasoning capabilities
reasoning-focused LLMs such as OpenAI o1 and DeepSeek-R1
optimizing full-length reasoning models into more concise reasoning models or directly training efficient reasoning models
dynamically reduces reasoning steps and length during inference
enhances reasoning efficiency based on input prompt properties such as difficulty or length control
hypothesised intrinsic minimum number of tokens required for successful problem-solving on a task

figures.caption: An example of the “overthinking phenomenon”: when asked “Which is larger, 0.9 or 0.11?”, the reasoning model takes an unnecessarily long time (e.g., 19 seconds for QwQ-32B and 42 seconds for DeepSeek-R1) to arrive at the correct answer. This example was tested in March 2025.
figures.why: Side-by-side traces show re-checking after the answer is reached.

figures.caption: Overview of efficient reasoning methods, model-oriented, reasoning output-oriented, input prompts-oriented.
figures.why: Six approaches on one input-model-output pipeline.

figures.caption: A summary of prompts used with reasoning models to generate concise reasoning outputs.
figures.why: Verbatim prompt templates for TALE-EP, CoD, CCoT and token complexity.

figures.caption: Examples of efficient Best-of-N sampling methods.
